title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-sophia-wu
content:
Context:
- Local dev box + dockerized serving runtime hitting intermittent OOMs while loading and running 7B fp16 model.
- Symptoms: OOM during model load sometimes, sometimes during first forward. Not consistent.
- Suspected causes: driver/library mismatch, CUDA runtime vs driver, leftover cuda contexts, memory fragmentation, KV cache + large batch, torch+cuda build mismatch.

Commands / checks run (ordered chronological):
1) Check GPU + driver:
   $ nvidia-smi
   Wed Nov  5 11:02:12 2025
   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
   | GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
   |  0   A100-SXM-80GB      On   | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                  N/A |
   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
   Note: driver reports CUDA Version 12.1. But our container expects CUDA 11.x (libcudart.so.11.*). Potential mismatch.

2) Inside container: check cuda toolkit libs and torch CUDA version
   $ docker exec -it rtv /bin/bash
   # ls /usr/local/cuda*
   lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 14 Nov  1 /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8
   /usr/local/cuda-11.8/bin/nvcc -> present

   $ python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
   2.2.0
   11.8
   True

   So PyTorch built against CUDA 11.8 but host driver is 12.1. Usually upwards-compatible but sometimes minor driver/runtime mismatches produce weird failures.

3) Reproduce and capture stack trace:
   Error during load:
   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 79.90 GiB total capacity; 77.12 GiB already allocated; 1.00 GiB free; 76.85 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
   During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
   Traceback (most recent call last):
     File "/app/serve.py", line 212, in forward
       outputs = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False)
     File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1614, in _call_impl
       return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
     File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/transformers/generation_utils.py", line 1532, in generate
       output = self.model.generate(... )
   torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.00 GiB (GPU 0; 79.90 GiB total capacity; 77.12 GiB already allocated)

   Observations: "already allocated" is large. Could be residue from previous processes/contexts or memory leak.

4) Check processes and orphaned contexts:
   $ nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
   # shows PID 2345 (python) using 76GB, PID 3278 (docker) small 
   $ ps aux | grep python
   root     2345  8.9  7.2 /opt/venv/bin/python /app/serve.py --workers 1

   Killed and restarted container — OOM still reproducible after ~3 runs.

5) LDD and lib mismatch checks:
   $ python -c "import torch; import ctypes; print(ctypes.CDLL('libcudart.so').CUDA_RUNTIME_VERSION)" 
   # fails with OSError: libcudart.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory 
   Found libcudart.so.11.0 under /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64 but LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container is missing that path on some exec contexts.

6) dpkg/apt checks on host (for driver):
   $ dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia
   ii  nvidia-driver-535  535.54.03-0ubuntu1  amd64  NVIDIA driver metapackage

7) Reproduced a different failure on another dev box: "libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory" when docker base image used was slim and missing nvidia libs.

8) Tried diff fixes (notes):
   - Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container to /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64:/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib
     result: python sees libcudart, but still OOM during heavy ops.
   - Downgraded container CUDA symlink to /usr/local/cuda-12.1 to match driver (just symlink change), restarted container.
     result: Torch still reports torch.version.cuda == 11.8 (because wheel was built for 11.8). Changing symlink doesn't change torch binary compatibility. But ldd on libtorch shows it links to cuda 11 libs.
   - Installed pytorch wheel built for CUDA 12.1 (pip install torch==2.2.0+cu121 ...) inside container
     result: After switching to torch+cu121, immediate segfaults in some ops (likely cuDNN mismatch). Rolled back.
   - Tried using NVIDIA container toolkit (runtime= nvidia) vs host driver binder. Inconsistent differences.
   - Force garbage collect + torch.cuda.empty_cache() at key places. Helped a bit (reduced reserved memory) but did not eliminate growing reservation over multiple inferences.
   - Added with torch.no_grad() and model.eval() everywhere to ensure no extra graph build.
   - Lower batch size from 8 -> 2, drastically reduces OOM frequency. Pointing to batch/memory pressure root cause.

9) Hypotheses / root cause candidates:
   - Memory fragmentation + huge reserved blocks in PyTorch causing OOM despite free memory. PyTorch caching allocator reserves large chunks. empty_cache helps but not always.
   - Version mismatch between driver (12.x) and runtime libs (11.x) + cuDNN mismatch causing fallback code paths allocating more memory or failing in unexpected ways.
   - Memory leak / stateful KV cache: model.generate might keep past_key_values across calls if not cleared properly; confirm code path.
   - Multiple processes/shared CUDA context (gunicorn/workers) causing oversubscription of GPU memory. Need to ensure worker forking happens after CUDA init or use forkserver/spawn.
   - Docker image base missing proper cuda driver libs causing the runtime to use a compatibility shim that uses more memory.

10) Next steps / TODOs:
   - [ ] Reproduce minimal repro script that reliably triggers OOM in < 30s. Keep simple loop calling model.generate with controlled inputs.
   - [ ] Try spawn server process with PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1 and use torch.multiprocessing.set_start_method('spawn') to avoid context inheritance.
   - [ ] Build/pip-install a torch wheel that exactly matches host (try 11.8 to match container toolkit) OR use NVIDIA-provided CUDA 11.8 driver on host (but host requires 535.x). Check compatibility matrix: driver 535 supports CUDA 12+ and backwards compat to 11.8? (investigate).
   - [ ] Run python -m torch.utils.collect_env and attach output to TASK-987.
   - [ ] Check servicer code for accidental retention of past_key_values between requests; add explicit del past_key_values / gc.collect() / torch.cuda.empty_cache() after each request.
   - [ ] Add tracing: log torch.cuda.memory_reserved(), memory_allocated(), allocated tensors shapes at key points.
   - [ ] Try running with torch.compile disabled (some users reported compiled kernels leak memory with certain versions).

Random collected logs/snippets: 
- "Warning: Found no NVIDIA driver on your system. Please check that you have an NVIDIA GPU and installed a driver from https://www.nvidia.com/Download/index.aspx" (appears when running slim-cuda image)
- "Failed to load cuDNN from libcudnn.so.8: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "Expected CUDA runtime version 11.8 but detected 12.1" (from some container compatibility checks)

Notes to self: Keep separate branch with small docker image that contains exact torch+cuX wheel + cuda libs to ensure known-good reproducible environment. Avoid mixing host-installed driver expectations with container runtime symlink hacks. When debugging, reduce batch size and use OOM hooks to catch allocation site (TORCH_USE_CUDA_DUMP on newer builds?).

If stuck, ping @Asha and @Raja — they saw similar flaky OOMs on dedicated machines last quarter.

End of notes.
